messages:
lucy.marketing: Heads-up 1: we need aligned copy and timing for public comms about the morning issue. Also want to confirm what we put on the webinar registration page so attendees aren't surprised.

ben.support: Impact summary: elevated 5xx on text-gen endpoints from ~08:12-08:39 UTC. Some retries succeeded. We're pulling a list of customers with errors now.

kai.prod: Root cause still under investigation but we reverted to the last known good configuration at 08:39 and errors dropped immediately. No signs of data exfiltration.

oncall-bot: Incident INC-2026-043 created at 08:13 UTC: elevated 5xx on hosted text-generation endpoints. Mitigation applied at 08:39 UTC.

lucy.marketing: Thanks. Drafting suggestions below. Want short + neutral language for status page, a slightly longer customer email for affected accounts, and a tiny banner line for webinar pages. PTAL.

lucy.marketing: ```Status page short (proposed):
We experienced a brief service disruption affecting text-generation endpoints between 08:12 and 08:39 UTC. Mitigation was applied and services have returned to normal. If you continue to experience issues, please contact support and include request IDs and timestamps. We will publish a follow-up with technical details when available.

Customer email (affected accounts):
This morning, some requests to Redwood's text-generation API returned 5xx errors between 08:12 and 08:39 UTC. Our engineering team reverted to a known-good configuration and restored normal service; retries may have succeeded. We have found no evidence of customer data exposure. If you observed errors, please reply to this message or open a ticket with request IDs and timestamps so we can investigate impact on your usage.

Webinar banner copy (short):
Note: We experienced a brief service disruption earlier today that has been resolved. Services are operating normally. See our status page [link].
```

ben.support: That looks fine. A couple of legal asks: don't say "no evidence" without approval from security. Rachel, can you weigh in?

rachel.legal: Agree. Change to: "We have not identified any customer data exposure at this time." That limits liability. Also avoid any phrasing that implies root cause is fully understood.

kai.prod: Fine by ops. Updated status line: "Mitigation was applied" instead of "reverted" in the public status. Keep the email a bit more specific for customers.

lucy.marketing: Updated copy with legal tweak and ops wording.

lucy.marketing: ```Updated public status:
We experienced a brief service disruption affecting text-generation endpoints between 08:12 and 08:39 UTC. Mitigation was applied and services have returned to normal. We have not identified any customer data exposure at this time. We will publish a post-incident summary within 72 hours.

Updated webinar banner:
Note: brief disruption earlier today; service restored. More details on our status page [link].
```

tom.sales: Quick ask on leads: for webinar registrants who are also customers, AEs should be flagged to follow up. For pure prospects, no proactive email unless they explicitly report an issue. Sales will hold a short outreach script for any warm leads flagged by support.

ben.support: We're exporting affected-customer list now and will DM AEs for any accounts with confirmed errors. Support will send individualized emails to affected customers within 60 minutes.

lucy.marketing: Timing plan proposed: publish the short status update now, queue the webinar banner change for the next site deploy (ETA 2 hours), and send targeted customer emails within the hour. No public blog or social posts at this time. Any objections?

rachel.legal: No objections from legal. Just request to save the incident timeline for the post-incident report.

kai.prod: Ops: we'll hand off an incident timeline to post-incident doc.

oncall-bot: Update: INC-2026-043 status posted by lucy.marketing at 08:50 UTC.

lucy.marketing: I'll publish the status now and paste the link here once live. Thanks all 1: will draft a short internal note for comms and handoff to CS/Sales. :raised_hands:
